title: Alacritty fails or renders a blank window on an ARM Wayland graphics stack
body: I built Alacritty on Linux aarch64 under Wayland, but 0.12.0-dev exits with `Error: the requested context Api isn't supported.` The verbose log says it is using EGL 1.4. I also tried Alacritty 0.11.0; it detects a Mali-G78 and tries the OpenGL 3.3 renderer, but shader compilation fails because the compiler only supports up to version `320 es`.

symptoms_visible: My 0.12.0-dev build exits on Wayland with `the requested context Api isn't supported` after reporting EGL 1.4.
Alacritty 0.11.0 also does not start successfully; it selects the OpenGL 3.3 renderer and then reports that its shader compiler supports only version `320 es`.
N0.label: N0 ARM Wayland startup failures reported

symptoms_visible: After building and running the first proposed branch, Alacritty still does not work properly.
N1_x.label: N1_x first context branch aftermath

symptoms_visible: The proposed branch still does not run correctly on my Wayland session.
N2.label: N2 EGL and GLX capabilities collected

symptoms_visible: Changing the requested OpenGL ES context from 3.0 to 3.1 still does not make Alacritty work properly.
N3_x.label: N3_x GLES 3.1 context attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: The latest try-es3 branch opens a window and the zsh process accepts commands, but nothing is visible in the window.
The log reaches initialization complete and reports the OpenGL ES 2.0 renderer without an obvious error.
N4.label: N4 try-es3 starts but renders blank

symptoms_visible: The Wayland window remains completely blank, including when I run htop inside it.
Requesting OpenGL ES 3.1 and running with MESA_DEBUG=1 do not change the blank output or add an error to the debug log.
N5.label: N5 blank rendering confirmed without GL errors

symptoms_visible: The later debug-context branch initializes with the OpenGL ES 2.0 renderer, but its window is still blank and MESA_DEBUG=1 reports no graphics error.
N5_x.label: N5_x debug-context branch aftermath

symptoms_visible: When I clear WAYLAND_DISPLAY and run through the alternate display backend, the Alacritty terminal is visible and usable.
That working run reports GLX 1.4 and loads swrast_dri.so.
N6.label: N6 alternate display backend works

symptoms_visible: Alacritty displays a visible, usable terminal when I run it outside the broken Wayland rendering path by clearing WAYLAND_DISPLAY.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with working display-backend fallback

solution.intent: Build and test the first linked context-creation branch.
solution.concrete_example: Please build the linked branch and check whether it starts on this ARM Wayland system.

edges.comment: From c1-c2 on the reporter's system: participant1 asked the reporter to try the first linked branch; the reporter's screenshot and reply say it still did not work properly.

question_patterns: Could you provide the output of eglinfo?
What EGL version, vendor, client APIs, and Wayland configurations does eglinfo report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My Wayland eglinfo output says EGL API version 1.4, vendor ARM, version `1.4 Valhall-r23p0-01rel0`, and client APIs `OpenGL_ES`. The listed Wayland configurations are renderable through ES and ES2; GBM initialization fails.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My Wayland eglinfo reports a current Mesa stack with both desktop OpenGL and OpenGL ES, and the configurations support the requested desktop context.
The same ARM EGL 1.4 and OpenGL ES-only capabilities are reported, but GBM initialization succeeds.

question_patterns: Could you also provide the output of glxinfo?
Does glxinfo show an available GLX display and direct rendering?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My glxinfo output can connect to display `:0`, reports direct rendering `Yes`, and reports server GLX version 1.4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: glxinfo cannot open an X display at all, so there is no alternate GLX path available on this machine.

edges.comment: From c3-c4, entirely on the reporter's ARM laptop: participant1 requested eglinfo and glxinfo, and the reporter pasted their raw outputs. Interpretation of the capabilities remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Change the fallback context request from OpenGL ES 3.0 to OpenGL ES 3.1 and rebuild.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the one-line change from `ContextApi::Gles(3, 0)` to `ContextApi::Gles(3, 1)` on top of the branch and rebuild.

edges.comment: From c5-c6 on the reporter's system: the reporter applied the exact GLES 3.1 context patch, rebuilt, and reported that it still did not work properly.

solution.intent: Use the revised try-es3 renderer branch so OpenGL ES version strings are not mistaken for desktop GLSL and an appropriate GLES renderer can be selected.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the revised renderer patch that normalizes the shading-language version, avoids selecting desktop GLSL when the version contains `es`, and tries GLES-compatible contexts.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the shader compiler text and EGL capabilities. Recognizing that a lexicographic version check could classify an OpenGL ES shading-language string as desktop GLSL was participant1's engineering inference.

edges.comment: From c7-c11: once participant1 learned that 0.11.0 had never worked, a revised try-es3 patch was supplied. On the reporter's laptop it fixed the immediate startup failure and reached a working PTY, but the visible terminal remained completely blank, so it did not fully resolve the case.

question_patterns: Could you run the current branch with MESA_DEBUG=1 and report any additional output?
Could you test the alternate GLES context version in the source and say whether the blank rendering changes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I changed the version from 3.0 to 3.1, but nothing changed. Adding `MESA_DEBUG=1` also made no change and added no useful error to the debug log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: MESA_DEBUG reports a shader-link or invalid-operation error every time the blank frame is drawn.
The GLES 3.1 probe is still blank, and MESA_DEBUG only adds unrelated configuration warnings.

question_patterns: If you run htop inside the empty terminal, do any colored backgrounds appear?
Is all terminal content invisible, or can you see colored cells from a full-screen program?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot see anything when I run `htop` in the empty Alacritty window; it is still just blank.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: htop's colored backgrounds are visible, but glyphs and line art are missing.

edges.comment: From c12-c18 on the reporter's laptop: participant1 requested GLES-version, MESA_DEBUG, and colored-background probes. The reporter supplied only observed results. The reporter separately explained that updating Mesa was not feasible after an attempted upgrade broke.

solution.intent: Build and test the later linked branch with a debug graphics context and additional renderer changes.
solution.concrete_example: Build the later linked branch, run it with MESA_DEBUG=1, and check whether it renders or reports a graphics error.

edges.comment: From c19-c22 on the reporter's system: participant1 supplied another linked branch. It initialized successfully with GLES2 but remained blank, and neither its debug context nor MESA_DEBUG emitted an error.

question_patterns: Please test the alternate display backend by clearing WAYLAND_DISPLAY and tell me whether the terminal becomes visible.
Could you run the current build once without the Wayland display variable and report what you see?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Clearing `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` works for me. Alacritty opens with visible terminal content, so this gives me a way to run it on my laptop.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Clearing WAYLAND_DISPLAY still produces the same completely blank terminal.
The alternate backend renders correctly but starts a little more slowly.

question_patterns: What does the verbose graphics log report during the working alternate-backend run?
Please run the working backend with verbose GL logging and paste the loader and context lines.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The working run says `Using GLX 1.4`, loads `/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/dri/swrast_dri.so`, reports the OpenGL ES 2.0 renderer, enables dual-source blending, and reaches initialization complete.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The working run uses the Mali hardware driver through GLX rather than loading swrast.

edges.comment: From c23-c24, only the reporter's laptop is described: participant1 asked for separate backend and debug probes. The reporter reported that clearing WAYLAND_DISPLAY rendered correctly and pasted the raw GLX/swrast loader lines. The conclusion that this is software rendering and isolates the failure to the Wayland graphics path is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Use the verified alternate display backend as the practical workaround because the machine's old Wayland/EGL graphics path opens a window but does not render, while the GLX software path renders correctly.
solution.concrete_example: Launch Alacritty with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=` on this laptop. The verified run uses GLX and swrast and displays the terminal correctly. The exact Wayland-side driver or shader defect was not conclusively identified, and updating the graphics stack was not possible on this machine.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter's raw output only says that the Wayland run is blank and that the working run uses GLX and loads swrast_dri.so. Interpreting this as a Wayland/EGL-path incompatibility on an old ARM graphics stack, and recognizing swrast as software rendering without hardware acceleration, is engineer inference. The thread never proves whether Mesa, the compositor, shader handling, or attribute binding is the exact defect.

edges.comment: Resolution from c24-c27: the reporter confirmed that clearing WAYLAND_DISPLAY provides a usable Alacritty session and accepted it as a practical choice because the graphics stack could not be updated. Participant1 noted that the working GLX path loads swrast and therefore lacks hardware acceleration; no exact Wayland-side defect was proven.

solution.intent: Immediately try the alternate display backend and use it if it renders correctly, rather than repeatedly changing GLES context versions.
solution.concrete_example: Try launching once with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=`. If the terminal is visible there, use that backend as the workaround and capture its verbose graphics log to determine whether it is hardware-accelerated.

edges.comment: Shortcut answer from the opening state, required because the thread first went through several falsified patch attempts. It proposes the same alternate-backend test that ultimately produced a usable terminal, but must not declare success until the reporter verifies visible output.

satisfaction_conditions: Must distinguish the initial context-selection failure from the later blank-rendering failure: the GLES-aware branch starts Alacritty and its PTY, but the Wayland window still displays no terminal content.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: ARM EGL exposes OpenGL ES, the Wayland GLES2 run initializes without reported GL errors but remains entirely blank, and clearing WAYLAND_DISPLAY produces a visible GLX run.

Must describe the accepted diagnosis conservatively as a problem in this machine's old Wayland/EGL graphics path; the thread does not conclusively prove whether Mesa, the compositor, shader handling, or attribute binding is the precise defect.
Must recommend the reporter-verified alternate display backend as the practical workaround, while noting that the working log loads swrast and therefore does not provide hardware acceleration.

Must not present the first context branch, changing only GLES 3.0 to 3.1, the try-es3 renderer patch alone, or the later debug-context branch as a complete fix; each was tried and still left the application unusable or blank.
Must have the reporter verify that terminal content is visible on the alternate backend before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux user who can build Rust branches, apply source patches, run graphics diagnostics, change environment variables, and collect verbose logs, but is not a graphics-stack developer and cannot safely upgrade the laptop's old Mesa installation.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief, cooperative, and persistent; follows exact test instructions, shares screenshots and raw logs, asks what additional information would help, and accepts a practical workaround when system upgrades are unavailable.
